wayfarer.subject: a young Wayfarer on the road: travel coat, scarf, satchel with a little lantern clipped to the strap, pointing forward eagerly, ready for a bout

wick_tender.subject: a lamplighter in a long dark coat and brimmed hat, holding a tall brass wick-pole with a lit flame at its tip, calm and proud

courier.subject: a cheerful road courier with a cap, a bulging parcel satchel and a rolled map, one hand on hip, grinning; mustard-yellow and brick-red clothes, the rolled map held up, no lantern

moss_warden.subject: a woodland gardener-warden in a mossy green smock and wide straw hat with flowers tucked in the band, holding a trowel, kind smile

fen_folk.subject: a fen-wader in tall waders and an oilskin coat, holding a lantern on a pole, reeds in the hat band, cheerful and weathered

net_hand.subject: a harbour fisher with a coiled net over one shoulder, a knitted cap, sleeves rolled, salty and cheerful; navy and sea-blue striped jumper, teal knitted cap, a net with cork floats over the shoulder, no lantern

miner.subject: a miner with a brass helmet-lamp shining, soot-smudged cheeks, a pickaxe over one shoulder, sturdy and friendly

kite_hand.subject: a windswept highland kite-hand with brass goggles pushed up, a long scarf streaming sideways, holding a small kite spool and string

frost_ward.subject: a frost-walker bundled in a fur-lined hood, thick mittens and snow boots, breath steaming, holding up a frosted lantern

troupe_player.subject: a travelling theatre player in a patched velvet cape, holding a comedy mask on a stick, mid-bow, theatrical

sky_watcher.subject: a star-watcher in a deep blue robe patterned with little stars, holding a brass spyglass, dreamy

sun_keeper.subject: a sun-keeper in warm golden robes and a sun-disc pendant, holding a sun-lantern high, serene and bright

junior.subject: an excited child stargazer in a too-big coat with a toy telescope, standing on tiptoe, big grin

acolyte.subject: a Hollowing acolyte: a calm, solemn figure in a hooded ash-grey robe holding a lantern with its shutter half-closed (a soft dim glow); gentle and sad, never villainous, face visible in the hood

runner.subject: a downhill wax-road runner in a padded jacket, goggles on the forehead, knee pads, a little runner sled-board under one arm, eager grin

brisa.subject: BRISA TALLOW, the first Lampwarden (Tinderwick, Ember): read her look from the references; she raises a glowing ember-lantern, warm and proud

reyl.subject: REYL WASH, the Tide Lampwarden of Pearlmoor: an old weathered ferryman in an oilskin coat and cap, grey beard, rope coiled at his belt, steady and gruff with a kind eye

sable.subject: SABLE QUILL, the Verdant Lampwarden of Lowleaf: read her look from the reference; holding a leafy quill-staff, poised

otho.subject: OTHO GRIST, the Lampwarden of Cinderhead's mine: read his look from the reference; broad, soot and ember, a heavy miner's lamp held out

mira.subject: MIRA VAEL, the Storm Lampwarden of Galehigh: read her look from the references; wind-whipped, a kite-lantern on a line

ysolde.subject: YSOLDE FROST, the Frost Lampwarden of Pale Vault: read her look from the reference; cool, poised, a crystal lantern

lucan.subject: LUCAN PYRE, the Solar Lampwarden: read his look from the references; grand, theatrical, a sunburst lantern

nessa.subject: NESSA COLE, the Lunar Lampwarden of Nightreach: read her look from the references; quiet, reverent, a moon-lantern

wren.subject: WREN, the player's rival and friend: read their look from the reference; eager, competitive grin, lantern raised in challenge

cor.subject: WARDEN CÒR, gentle leader of the Hollowing: read their look from the references; tall, robed, a lantern held low and dimmed, sorrowful dignity, never cartoonish

fenn.subject: STAR-TENDER FENN, the player's old mentor: read his look from the references; elderly, kindly, a brass star-lamp and a long coat

georgina.subject: GEORGINA the Cat-keeper, a cheerful 'sunshine goth': read her look from the reference; a small dragon-cat perched on her shoulder

paul.subject: PAUL, read his look from the reference exactly (a real person's cameo, keep him warm and recognisable); a confident friendly grin, ready for a bout

esra.subject: WICK-MOTHER ESRA, a Starfall Vigilant: an elderly wick-maker in a long shawl, braids of wax-wick at her belt, a candle-lantern

bramm.subject: OLD FOREMAN BRAMM, a Starfall Vigilant: an old mining foreman, white moustache, helmet-lamp, a heavy hammer, gruff and fond

ondra.subject: ONDRA VAEL, a Starfall Vigilant of the high winds: a veteran kite-flier in a storm cloak with a great kite-lantern behind her

solenne.subject: DAME SOLENNE, a Starfall Vigilant of the sun: a stately older woman in gold and white robes, a sunburst halo-lantern

mer.subject: WARDEN MER, a Starfall Vigilant who once walked with the Hollowing: an elder in a grey hooded robe trimmed with silver stars, a lantern relit

heckler.subject: THE HECKLER of a cosy comedy lighthouse: same build as the reference man, in a rumpled checked suit and a squashed bowler hat, cupping one hand to his mouth to heckle, cheeky grin

usher.subject: THE USHER of a cosy comedy lighthouse theatre: same build as the reference man, in a smart burgundy usher's uniform with brass buttons and a pillbox cap, holding out a ticket and a small torch

juggler.subject: THE JUGGLER: the young person from the reference in a bright patchwork tunic and pointed shoes, juggling three coloured balls in an arc above their head, delighted

pie_thrower.subject: THE PIE-THROWER: the market trader from the reference in a baker's apron and floppy chef's hat, winding up to throw a custard pie, mischievous

critic.subject: THE CRITIC: the old woman from the reference in a severe purple coat with a lorgnette (opera glasses on a stick) raised to one eye and a notebook, one eyebrow arched, secretly amused

player_front.subject: the young lamp-tender's apprentice from the references (same hair, same green coat and satchel), front-facing, holding up a small glowing brass vesperlamp, confident (used for THE MIRROR, who wears your face)

punchwheel.subject: MR. PUNCHWHEEL, a clockwork brass joke-machine automaton with a big grinning brass face-plate (dial eyes, rosy cheeks, waxed moustache, toothy grin), a winding key in its head, a red pleated bellows body on a little wheeled brass base, one spindly arm raised like a showman; cheeky, never creepy
